newsitem.title: TURKEY: Islamist Turk PM narrowly survives censure motion.
newsitem.headline: Islamist Turk PM narrowly survives censure motion.

text.p: Turkey's parliament on Tuesday voted by a slender majority to drop a censure motion filed against Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan and his cabinet by the secularist opposition, speaker Mustafa Kalemli said.
MPs voted 271-265 to drop the motion, which criticised the Islamist-conservative government for straying from the country's 73-year-old secularist path.
"Therefore the debate on the censure motion has been rejected," Kalemli told parliament.
A number of MPs from the government -- which has 280 seats in the 550-seat house -- defected to the opposition in the vote, but Erbakan's alliance had the support of a small far-right Islamist party.
The government has been embroiled in a row with the powerful, secularist military -- which was strongly backed by the mainstream media -- over Islamist activism.

Government MPs had predicted the motion would be thrown out, and after the vote, they were confident they would be left alone by the opposition -- which had filed three unsuccessful censure motions before -- for a while.
"From our point of view it was an expected result -- we said it wasn't going work. We are continuing on our path," said conservative minister Ufuk Soylemez.
But despite the victory the government faces an uncertain future, with dissident government MPs trying to craft an Islamist-free coalition formula with the fractious opposition.
